source_citations.excerpt: **Criterion:** `handy settings get [KEY]` returns all non-secret settings or one key; `handy settings keys` lists settable keys with type, allowed values or range and read-only flag; `handy settings set KEY VALUE` changes one scalar setting. source_citations.excerpt: **Criterion:** Settings carry a persisted revision number returned by every read and incremented by 1 on every committed write from any surface, including writes made by Handy itself; a write that changes nothing and a read do not increment it. Writes accept `--expected-revision N`; a mismatch returns `revision_conflict` with the current revision in `error.details.current_revision` and writes nothing. All writers (UI commands, a running instance and a headless CLI process) are serialized by one cross-process settings lock, and each writer re-reads the stored settings under that lock before applying its change, so a write without expected revision applies to the latest settings and never discards fields changed by another writer.

conclusions.rationale: The supplied architecture covers private live routing, owner/store identity, live effects and UI notification, passive older-version refusal, offline startup fencing, the 5-second end-to-end deadline, unknown timeout outcome and no blind retry/fallback. It does not specify the offline capability check which rejects operations requiring live state with unavailable instead of applying them through the offline adapter. The test-only live domain mention is not that routing rule. This missing detail is batch-local.

source_citations.excerpt: **Criterion:** When a Handy instance of the same user and settings store is running, the CLI sends the operation to it over a local channel accessible only to that user and waits up to 5 seconds for its answer; the instance applies it with its live state, re-registers affected shortcuts and notifies its UI. If no answer arrives in time, the CLI returns `unavailable` with `error.details.outcome` set to `unknown`, and agents must read again before retrying. If a running Handy without this channel (an older version) is detected, the CLI returns `unavailable` and never writes the store itself. When none is running, the CLI applies the operation to the settings store itself under the same lock and validation. Operations that need live state (for example the current destination) return `unavailable` without a running instance. No network listener and no MCP server are introduced.

findings.description: Linux session DBus and Windows session/desktop singleton probes cannot by themselves establish absence in another session of the same user/store.
